gen_risks.description: Regional instability and ongoing conflict in South Sudan could cause further massive refugee inflows into Uganda, overburdening public services and water infrastructure in host districts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement long-term sustainable water and sanitation infrastructure in host districts and establish joint coordination mechanisms with OPM and UNHCR.
gen_risks.evidence: The most critical risk to this outlook is regional instability, particularly from the ongoing conflict in South Sudan.

gen_risks.description: High climate variability, severe droughts, and intense precipitation leading to floods could damage water infrastructure and threaten raw water sources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate resilience into engineering designs, construct water source protection buffer zones, and implement catchment reforestation and soil conservation.
gen_risks.evidence: high climate variability and underdeveloped water resources infrastructure could result in significant water stress in areas of the country.

gen_risks.description: Low dry-season water flows in the Namatala River could cause water deficits in Mbale Town and fail to satisfy required environmental flows for downstream ecosystems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct an Augmented Water Supply Study prior to construction to evaluate and implement storage impoundment, supplementary boreholes, or Manafwa system expansion.
gen_risks.evidence: Namatala’s dry weather flows in some cases may not be sufficient to meet projected water demand and maintain an adequate EF.

gen_risks.description: Weaknesses in procurement and contract management across implementing agencies could lead to processing delays, contract variations, and cost/time overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit dedicated procurement consultants, establish Project Support Teams, and deliver specialized training on World Bank procurement regulations and FIDIC contract management.
gen_risks.evidence: weakness... resulted in multiple amendments during contract implementation resulting in cost and time overruns.

gen_risks.description: Incomplete needs assessments and insufficient geotechnical studies during early design phases could cause major design changes and costly variations during civil works.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate comprehensive geotechnical studies and outcome-based needs assessments during the feasibility and detailed design stages prior to bidding.
gen_risks.evidence: incomplete needs assessments and inadequate attention to geotechnical studies leading to design changes/variations during implementation

gen_risks.description: Limited technical and financial capacity among domestic contractors for complex water infrastructure works could cause construction delays or poor execution quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Package contracts appropriately for market capacity, conduct wider market sounding/dissemination, and encourage joint ventures with capable international firms.
gen_risks.evidence: limited capacity of domestic contractors to conduct projects of this nature, complexity, and scope

gen_risks.description: Delay in fully operationalizing the IFMS project module at MWE and irregular internal audit sharing increase risks of financial reporting inaccuracies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Fully operationalize the IFMS project module at MWE, retain qualified accounting staff, and submit quarterly internal audit reports to the World Bank.
gen_risks.evidence: the project module of the IFMS has not been fully operationalized at the MWE, which increases the risk of errors and inaccuracy

gen_risks.description: Land acquisition and involuntary economic or physical displacement along pipeline routes and facility sites could trigger community grievances and civil works delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare and implement site-specific Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs), ensure prompt compensation payments, and establish dedicated project grievance redress mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: road encroachment and potential works like plants, pump stations and storage tanks may have land acquisition implications and displacement

gen_risks.description: Influx of external construction labor into project host communities could lead to social disruption, health risks, and potential gender-based violence (GBV).
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce mandatory worker codes of conduct, maximize local workforce hiring, implement labor influx management plans, and conduct community/worker GBV awareness training.
gen_risks.evidence: The proposed project will apply upmost due diligence in the management and monitoring of labor influx to minimize any potential GBV in Project areas.

gen_risks.description: Newly designated Umbrella Water Authorities (UWAs) may face initial operating losses and revenue deficits in small towns, threatening long-term operation and maintenance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce tariff guidelines that cover full operating costs plus a 25% margin, automate cost-indexed tariff adjustments, and build UWA commercial management capacity.
gen_risks.evidence: Several of the systems will show operating losses in the first years of operation, but these losses will gradually decrease as production increases.

gen_risks.description: High population pressure, poor agricultural land use, and wetland encroachment in catchments cause soil erosion and siltation, degrading raw water source quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement sub-catchment management plans focusing on soil and water conservation, riverbank revegetation, buffer zone protection, and alternative community livelihoods.
gen_risks.evidence: high population pressure, poor land use management practices, and wetland encroachment are leading to excessive land degradation and water quality and quantity challenges

gen_risks.description: Mishandling of existing Asbestos Cement (AC) pipes during system rehabilitation poses serious environmental, occupational, and public health hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce strict asbestos management protocols in ESMPs for safe removal, packaging, transport, and disposal in compliance with NEMA guidelines.
gen_risks.evidence: improper handling of asbestos cement (AC) pipes, OHS risks

gen_risks.description: Delays by the Government of Uganda in making timely counterpart funding contributions for land acquisition and RAP compensations could stall civil works implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Ensure GoU allocates adequate counterpart funds in annual sector budget allocations and track release schedules prior to contract execution.
gen_risks.evidence: The GoU will be responsible for providing US$8 million in counterpart financing to cover... acquisition of land, and any compensation

gen_risks.description: Inadequate coordination among multiple implementing departments, local authorities, and humanitarian agencies could lead to redundant infrastructure or improper site placement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize MWE's Sector Liaison Department for central coordination, engage a Project Support Team, and streamline planning through the Water and Environment Sector Working Group.
gen_risks.evidence: In Uganda, a lack of coordination resulted in boreholes being drilled too close to each other or too close to shallow pit latrines

gen_risks.description: Taking over management of financially unviable small towns with high operating costs could strain NWSC's cash flow and compromise capital investment capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply standard due diligence assessments prior to town transfers, enforce automatic tariff indexation, and maintain a sustainable balance of grant and on-lending financing.
gen_risks.evidence: The NWSC, however, is hesitant to take on additional debt given that its projected cash flow is earmarked for implementing a 10-year capital investment plan

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk: as detailed in the CPF, significant political uncertainty is not foreseen, but governance and effective public-sector management present substantial risks.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will mitigate these risks through (a) strengthening the MWE's regulatory framework; (b) carrying out a citizen engagement strategy; and (c) strengthening project implementation efforts in close coordination with local government officials and development partners. The World Bank's procurement processes will also help safeguard the Project from corruption.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risk: the Umbrella Water Authority (UWA) as a regional service delivery model for small towns and RGCs was recently introduced. Although the decision to scale up this model was informed by extensive analytical work and a pilot project, the UWA model was only recently operationalized.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will support implementation of a professionalized monitoring system focused on enhancing revenue collection approaches (billing software, cashless/mobile payment systems) and on strengthening integration of specialized private operators through improved contract management. The implementation team will use the Utility Performance Monitoring and Information System (UPMIS) tool to regularly review UWA and NWSC performance.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk: the Procurement risk is rated Substantial while the FM risk is Moderate. The risks identified relate to delays and skills gaps at different stages of procurement processing.
gt_risks.mitigation: IWMDP will benefit from the lessons learned and mechanisms put in place under the predecessor project (WMDP); detailed mitigation measures for the procurement risk are set out in the Appraisal (Procurement) section.

gt_risks.description: The environmental and social risk is deemed Substantial given (a) potential opposition to the introduction of a new service delivery model, including new tariffs and catchment management measures; (b) the influx of new workers in small towns and RGCs; and (c) potentially adverse environmental impacts from the construction and operation of the proposed investments.
gt_risks.mitigation: The environmental and social risk will be managed through the application of an Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and related safeguards instruments (Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, Resettlement Action Plans).

gt_risks.description: Other risks (social tensions in districts hosting refugees): tensions between refugees and citizens are caused by inequity in access to and payment for water supply and sanitation (WSS) services. While refugees in the settlements benefit from humanitarian aid and GoU support, Ugandans in host communities receive limited support for services and infrastructure, causing social tension that may result in Project implementation delays given potential community opposition to the works.
gt_risks.mitigation: The GoU has prioritized development efforts for poor districts hosting refugees while remaining firmly committed to its policy on refugee protection. The Project will manage this risk by designing WSS facilities and catchment management measures that benefit both host communities and refugees, and by ensuring the Project's social and communication management plan is applied and adequately supervised. There are no known existing risks to the refugee protection framework or reputational risks for the Project.
